summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators have become the dominant way corporations consume foundation models, offering access to multiple model families (GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more) through a single secure managed API that keeps data inside the customer's cloud boundary. In 2026 the landscape is led by the three hyperscalers — AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI — with data-platform players (Snowflake Cortex, Databricks) and enterprise-governance specialists (IBM watsonx, Oracle) gaining ground. There is no single winner; the best fit is usually the aggregator that matches an organization's existing cloud contracts, compliance posture, and data gravity.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay within the enterprise's own cloud tenancy/VPC and chosen region, and are not used to train the underlying vendor models.

Compliance and governance: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR/EU data boundary) plus centralized audit logging, IAM, and guardrails that raw vendor APIs don't provide out of the box.

Consolidated billing and existing contracts: usage rolls into an existing cloud commitment (EDP, MACC, committed-use discounts), avoiding new vendor procurement, separate invoices, and net-new security reviews.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in: a single API surface lets teams swap between Claude, Llama, Mistral, GPT, Gemini, etc. as price/performance shifts, without rewriting integrations for each vendor.

Enterprise integration: native connection to the company's data (warehouses, vector stores, identity), networking (PrivateLink/VPC), and tooling reduces engineering effort versus stitching together individual vendor APIs.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens by model, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through existing Azure/MACC commitments.
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-centric enterprises wanting first-party OpenAI models with enterprise security and Azure integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing by model, Batch, and Provisioned Throughput (reserved model units); billed via existing AWS EDP.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native organizations that want the broadest third-party model catalog (especially Anthropic Claude) with deep AWS integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-token (character/token) pricing plus GSU (Generative Scale Units) for provisioned throughput — e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields ~67,250 tokens/sec sustained; committed-use discounts available.
key_features: Grounding and RAG with Vertex AI Search
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud / data-analytics-heavy enterprises wanting Gemini plus a large open-model garden and provisioned throughput at scale.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits (per-token LLM functions and Cortex compute); folds into existing Snowflake spend.
key_features: Models run next to governed data in Snowflake (no data movement)
Role-based access control and data masking
platforms.best_for: Organizations with data gravity in Snowflake wanting to run LLMs directly against governed warehouse data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
available_models: Third-party open models from Hugging Face catalog
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) consumption and token-based pricing; available on IBM Cloud, on-prem, and hybrid; subscription and committed options.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and audit
Granite open-source models with IP indemnification
platforms.best_for: Highly regulated enterprises and governments needing hybrid/on-prem deployment with strong AI governance.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI (Foundation Model APIs)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based pay-per-token plus provisioned throughput, billed via Databricks DBUs on the customer's cloud.
key_features: Models served next to lakehouse data
MLflow and AI Gateway for audit/rate-limiting
platforms.best_for: Data/ML teams on the lakehouse wanting unified governance across custom and foundation models.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
available_models: OpenAI / other models via OCI integrations
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-character/token and dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; billed via OCI Universal Credits.
key_features: Integration with Oracle apps and Autonomous Database
platforms.best_for: Oracle ERP/database customers and sovereignty-focused buyers wanting GenAI close to Oracle data and apps.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: Various open-source models at the edge
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-neuron/token with a generous free tier; billed via Cloudflare account.
key_features: Serverless inference at the edge (low latency)
AI Gateway for caching, rate-limiting, and logging
platforms.best_for: Developers and companies needing low-latency, globally distributed edge inference with open models rather than heavy regulated workloads.
